//: TypeScript — incremental adoption, decision D8 (see DECISIONS.md).
MEASURED BEFORE CHOOSING (this is why checkJs is off, not an oversight):
checkJs off, strict on .ts/.tsx only ..... 0 errors
Turning checkJs on would mean editing nearly every source file to satisfy
the compiler, which contradicts milestone M1's own definition of done
('CI passes on the baseline with zero source changes') and would put a
large, untested diff through a working financial engine for no user
benefit. So: legacy .js is compiled but not checked; every NEW file is
.ts/.tsx and is checked under full strict mode.
The 128 figure is a burn-down metric, not a backlog to clear in one go.
Files stop contributing to it as they convert, per D8's staged plan.
'any' is prohibited in new code (see CONTRIBUTING.md). Nullable financial
values are explicitly `number | null` — never optional-and-assumed, because
an assumed-present price is exactly how a NaN reaches a ranking.
